# Independent audit of the balanced active-pair negative flux

The completed note `candidate ae6d727221cffaef`
passes independent audit without correction. Its exact verifier passes.
The geometry, cap probabilities, edge flows, and conditional-index
formulas were also recomputed independently with Fraction arithmetic.

## 1. Exact mixed support and normalization

The two endpoint triangles have area 13/4 and centroids (+/-1/12,0).
The exact fiber of their lifted convex hull at continuous base t is
((1-t)/2)(-K)+((1+t)/2)K. Thus the only integer fibers are -K,B,K,
with B=(K-K)/2; no additional fiber appears and no endpoint section
is enlarged.

The six listed vertices of B are precisely the nonzero pairwise
half-differences of the three triangle vertices. They form the stated
hexagon, whose area is 39/8. Hence M=91/8. All three fibers are full
two-dimensional bodies, so intrinsic H_2 is their ordinary area sum.
The convex hull is full-dimensional in R^3 and centrally symmetric.

## 2. Global depth and all closed halfspaces

The origin is a point of the middle fiber. A closed ambient halfspace
containing it and its reflection cover the full ambient space. Reflection
preserves the mixed measure, proving mass at least M/2 for every such
halfspace, with no exclusion of vertical normals or boundary mass.

The two x-coordinate caps have zero boundary area in every fiber.
Symmetry gives each mass M/2, so both are actual active caps at the
origin. For every point of the mixed set, the two opposite caps with
that fixed continuous normal through the point have masses summing to M;
one has mass at most M/2. Consequently the origin is a global maximizer
and the maximum normalized depth is exactly one half.

In fact every nonvertical through-origin cap has mass M/2. Thus activity
is with respect to the complete ambient halfspace family, not a restricted
set of normals.

## 3. Sections, Jacobians, and balance

At x=0, the endpoint sections both have length 18/13 and the middle
section has length two. Their total coarea section factor is 62/13,
since the continuous normal has length one. All sections are centered
vertically, and the equal endpoint lengths occur at opposite integer
indices. Their full ambient centroid is exactly the origin.

The middle line passes through the top and bottom vertices of B but
also through its interior. Those endpoint contacts have zero one-dimensional
section-boundary measure and do not obstruct the first variation. The
normal derivatives vanish, both from the section moments and directly
from symmetry. The opposite unit normals balance with equal positive
weights; their equal section factors give coarea-gradient balance as well.
No tilted ambient-plane volume Jacobian is used in place of the actual
within-fiber section measure.

## 4. Exact negative flux and conditional index

The positive cap in K has area 81/52 and fraction 81/169. Its reflected
endpoint has fraction 88/169. The middle fraction is one half. For the
normal x, both directed consecutive-edge flows are 13/48. Hence

    J=(13/48)[(1/2-88/169)+(81/169-1/2)]
     =-7/624.

Reversing the cap reverses both the scalar means and the probability
differences, so the opposite cap has exactly the same flux. Each normalized
flux is J/M=-1/1014. Equal-weight averaging therefore remains negative;
the unweighted sum is -7/312. There is no omitted middle mean contribution,
because that mean is zero.

For |t|<1, the scalar section factors are

    f_1=(18-8t)/13,
    f_(-1)=(18+8t)/13,
    f_0=2-8|t|/13.

Thus the conditional integer mean is -16t/(62-8|t|), with derivative
-8/31 at zero. The profile J(t)=(32t^2-7)/624 and correction
R(t)=-4t/39 satisfy J'=-R. In particular R(0)=0 and the section centroid
is zero, while J(0) is strictly negative. Values at the extreme endpoints
t=+/-1 may be taken from the coarea representative; the decreasing
conditional-mean conclusion uses only a neighborhood of zero.

## 5. Strength and remaining limitation

This example has a balanced pair of actual active equal-budget caps at
an actual global depth maximizer. It therefore removes the earlier
nonactive-opposite-cap caveat. Closed-cap coverage, raw normal balance,
coarea-gradient balance, and full section-centroid stationarity do not
force the flux sum to be nonnegative.

Its normalized depth is one half, above the OC target. It is not an
extremum minimizing optimal depth over convex bodies. No assertion about
such an additional hypothesis or a below-target budget is refuted here.

The separate note `candidate 02ab05d91af31cbf` also
passes audit in its corrected scope: every other fiber must have zero
cap mass. Its raw-normal balance argument and the explicit positive
trapezoid-circuit calculation are valid. Merely placing the other fiber
barycenters outside the caps does not suffice; that extension was removed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
